title: Ιn vivo imaging of DNA-bound minichromosome maintenance complex in embryonic mouse cortex
protocol: Expose pregnant mice to lethal overdose of isoflurane and euthanize by cervical dislocation.
Section the abdomen to reveal the uterus.
Remove the uterine horns and place them in cold PBS 1×.
Carefully remove the embryos from their yolk sac and isolate their heads.
Clean the isolated tissues by performing 3 PBS 1× washes.
Put a 48-well plate on ice and add 500 μL of LMA 3% while still in liquid form (45°C).
Wait 1 min until the temperature becomes tolerable.
Remove the excess liquid from each tissue using a perforated spoon and a piece of absorbent paper (∼40°C).
Place the tissue in the well and gently swirl with a pipette tip until the tissue is totally covered with LMA.
Place the tissue at the appropriate orientation carefully and support with the pipette tip until LMA starts to solidify.
Leave the 48-well plate on ice until LMA is completely solid and afterwards place it at 4°C for 30 min.
Remove the embedded tissue from the 48-well plate by gently sliding a micro spatula toward the well circumference until the embedded tissue springs out.
Create a trapezoid shape of the embedded tissue with a scalpel so that its larger base touches the vibratome plate and smaller base faces the vibratome blade for coronal sections at the cortex level.
Stabilize the embedded tissue on the vibratome platform using a thin layer of instant glue to prevent displacement by the vibratome blade.
Wait 2 minutes until the glue is dried.
Place the vibratome plate in the tank with screwdrivers.
Fill the tank with cold PBS 1× to fully cover the sample.
Cut serial sections of 250 μm thickness using a vibratome.

Adjust the speed and frequency according to the developmental stage studied: for later embryonic stages (E14.5 to E18.5), set the speed at 0.225 mm/s and frequency at 50 Hz; for earlier stages (E10.5 to E12.5) and smaller tissues, set the speed at 0.125 mm/s and frequency at 70 Hz.
Prepare a 24-well plate with cold PBS 1× and keep it on ice.
Collect consecutive sections of the brain using thin paint brushes.
Place each collected section in separate wells of the 24-well plate on ice.
Handle tissue sections gently to avoid damage.
Select sections that include the dorsal cortex.
Keep the selected sections moist throughout the protocol.
Incubate the sections in freshly prepared CSK buffer for 20 minutes on ice.
Wash the sections once with cold PBS on ice.
Fix the sections with PFA 4% for 30 minutes at 20°C–23°C.
Wash the sections once with cold PBS on ice.
Keep control samples by skipping the CSK buffer incubation and immediately fixing them with PFA 4%.
Perform immunofluorescence staining in multiwell plates by removing and filling wells containing sections with appropriate solutions.
Wash floating sections with PBT-BSA 1% three times, the first two washes at 4°C and the last one at 20°C–23°C.
Incubate sections in PBS-Triton 0.5% for 20 minutes at 20°C–23°C.
Wash with PBT-BSA 1% three times at 4°C for at least 30 minutes each.
Block sections in blocking solution (1% FBS in PBT) for at least 1 hour at 20°C–23°C.
Wash with PBT-BSA 1% for at least 30 minutes at 4°C.
Incubate sections with EdU detection solution at 20°C–23°C for 30 minutes, protecting from light.
Wash sections with PBT three times at 4°C for at least 30 minutes each.
Incubate sections with the primary antibody against MCM2 (dilution 1:500 in blocking solution) for 16 hours at 4°C.
Remove the primary antibody solution after incubation.
Wash sections with PBT three times at 4°C for at least 2 hours each.
Incubate with fluorescent secondary antibody (dilution 1:1,000 in blocking solution) for 16 hours at 4°C.
Remove the secondary antibody solution.
Wash the sections with PBT at 4°C three times for at least 30 minutes each.
Perform nuclear DNA staining with DAPI (dilution 1:1,500 in PBS 1×) for 7 minutes at 20°C–23°C.
Wash the sections with PBT at 4°C three times for at least 30 minutes each.
Add a drop of PBS 1× on a microscope slide.
Transfer the sections using thin paint brushes and sharp forceps.
Remove excess PBS with absorbent paper.
Add Mowiol 4-88 solution to fully cover the section (60–100 μL per section).
Gently place a coverslip over the section.
Keep slides horizontally at 20°C–23°C until Mowiol is polymerized.
Store slides at 4°C for long-term storage.
Use a confocal system equipped with a fluorescent microscope for imaging mounted brain sections.
Focus on the dorsal cortex using at least a 63× high NA oil immersion lens.
Acquire images with an electronic zoom of 3 or higher and a resolution of at least 1,024 × 1,024 pixels.
Confirm that soluble proteins have been sufficiently removed while DNA-bound proteins remain intact on the tissue.
In sections incubated with CSK, cells in S phase (distinguished as EdU+) exhibit distinct patterns of nuclear MCM2 staining, representing recruitment of MCM complexes at origins of DNA replication.
Cells in sections without CSK show uniform nuclear staining for MCM2, corresponding to both bound and soluble fractions of MCM proteins.
Acquire serial z-stacks with a step size of 0.7 μm.
Set the total z-volume to 7.608 μm.
Set the pinhole to 1 Airy unit.
Quantify fluorescent intensity per nucleus using ImageJ.
Use the subtract background plugin in ImageJ with a rolling ball radius equal to the average size of nuclei.
